brand.name: The Fate of the Missing Persons
brand.fullName: The Fate of the Missing Persons: Humanitarian Dialogue and Cooperation
brand.subtitle: Humanitarian Dialogue and Cooperation

hero.lead: An international platform to exchange experience on missing persons, strengthen cooperation and discuss practical approaches to supporting their families.
hero.languages: Armenian and English with simultaneous interpretation

about.title: About the Conference
about.p1: The lack of information about missing persons leaves their families facing prolonged uncertainty. Addressing this humanitarian issue requires coordinated action, reliable national mechanisms and sustained international cooperation.
about.p2: The conference in Yerevan brings together representatives of public institutions, international and humanitarian organizations, the expert community and civil society to exchange experience and advance practical cooperation.
about.objectivesText: The conference aims to strengthen national capacities to address cases of missing persons through international and regional knowledge exchange, dialogue and cooperation. Discussions will focus on clarifying the fate of missing persons and addressing the rights and support needs of their families.

themes.title: Discussion Themes
themes.lead: The discussions are expected to support knowledge exchange, strengthen cooperation between national institutions and international partners, and inform practical recommendations for further work.

items.1: The scope of the issue and current challenges
items.2: Legal and institutional mechanisms for truth and justice
items.4: Families, memory, support and international cooperation

programme.title: Programme
programme.lead: The two-day programme includes an opening session, thematic discussions, international knowledge exchange and joint work on support to families and future cooperation.

items.openingDetails:
The Opening Ceremony will mark the official launch of the event, featuring welcome remarks and introductory statements by distinguished guests. It will outline the purpose and objectives of the conference and emphasize the humanitarian importance of clarifying the fate and whereabouts of missing persons.

• H.E. Nikol Pashinyan, Prime Minister of the Republic of Armenia
• H.E. Alen Simonyan, Secretary of the Security Council of the Republic of Armenia
• H.E. Ararat Mirzoyan, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Trade of the Republic of Armenia
• Ms. Mirjana Spoljaric Egger, President of the International Committee of the Red Cross (pre-recorded speech)
items.session1: Session I – The Scope of the Problem and the Realistic Image
items.session1Details:
This panel will discuss the scope and scale of the missing persons’ issue, providing a historical overview and examining available statistics to establish a realistic picture of the problem. It will address the legal and technical challenges associated with clarifying the fate and whereabouts of missing persons, as well as the key obstacles to cooperation, information exchange, and coordinated efforts to achieve answers for affected families.

Panelists:
• Dr. Anahit Manasyan, Human Rights Defender of the Republic of Armenia
• Mr. Pierre Gentile, UN representative on the Committee of Missing Persons in Cyprus (CMP)
• Dr. Leonidas Pantelides, Representative of the Greek Cypriot Community on the Committee of Missing Persons in Cyprus (CMP)
• Mr. Andreas Kleiser, Director for Policy and Cooperation at the International Commission on Missing Persons (ICMP)
• Ms. Dena Fisher, Operations Coordinator for EURASIA Region (ICRC)
• Mr. Mels Shirvanyan, Head of the Department for the Investigation of Particularly Important Cases at the Investigative Committee of the Republic of Armenia
• Q&A

Moderator: Mr. Vrezh Kardumyan, Head of the Humanitarian Issues Division at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Trade of the Republic of Armenia
items.session2: Session II – Legal Framework on Missing Persons
items.session2Details:
This panel will examine the international legal framework governing missing persons under International Humanitarian Law (IHL) and International Human Rights Law (IHRL), focusing on States’ obligations to prevent disappearances, search for missing persons, clarify their fate and whereabouts, and investigate cases of enforced disappearance and other unlawful disappearances. Experts will discuss State responsibility and accountability, the right of families to know the fate of their loved ones, access to justice and effective judicial and non-judicial remedies and reparations.

Drawing on international standards and comparative experience, the discussion will also highlight the role of families and civil society in transitional justice, reconciliation, and post-conflict recovery, identifying practical recommendations to strengthen cooperation among families, civil society, public authorities, and other relevant actors.

Panelists:
• Ms. Anna Karapetyan, Deputy Minister of Justice of the Republic of Armenia – Strengthening Legal and Institutional Frameworks for Missing Persons
• Mr. Gian Luca Beruto, Secretary General of International Institute of Humanitarian Law (IIHL) – Missing Persons in Armed Conflicts: the Role of Training, Dissemination and International Cooperation
• Prof. Gabriella Citroni, Professor of International Human Rights Law at the University of Milano-Bicocca; International Legal Advisor for FEDEFAM – The International Legal Framework for Missing Persons: Prevention, Search and Clarification of Fate and Whereabouts
• Dr. Yeghishe Kirakosyan, Ph.D., Director of International Courts and Arbitration LLM Program of Yerevan State University; Editor-in-Chief, Armenian Journal of International Law – State Responsibility for Violations Relating to Missing Persons
• Mr. Edoardo Gimigliano, Coordinator of Special Projects Department, International Institute of Humanitarian Law – Beyond Legal Compliance: Addressing Missing Persons as a Pathway to Reconciliation and Post-Conflict Recovery
• Ms. Anna Melikyan, Legal Expert in Human Rights and IHL; Project manager at Protection of Rights without Borders NGO – The Role of Civil Society and Families in Transitional Justice for Missing Persons
• Q&A

Moderator: Dr. Michael Riepl, Postdoctoral Researcher, Professor of International Law at the Academy for European Human Rights Protection, Germany
items.session3: Session III – Effective Measures for the Clarification of the Fate and Whereabouts of Missing Persons
items.session3Details:
This panel will draw on experiences from local and other contexts (Cyprus, Georgia, Iraq and Kuwait, the Western Balkans and the Americas) to explore how national, bilateral and multilateral mechanisms for clarifying the fate and whereabouts of missing persons were established and sustained. Presentations will examine mandates, institutional arrangements and operational approaches, including how they secure long-term resources, foster technical expertise and enable cooperation. The panel will also explore how unified registries, coordinated information management and the application of good forensic sciences contribute to the search for and identification of missing persons.

• Dr. Arthur Petrosyan, Acting Director of the Scientific Practical Center of Forensic Medicine, Ministry of Health – “Lessons learnt from Armenia”
• Mr. Pierre Gentile, UN representative in the Committee on Missing Persons in Cyprus (CMP); Dr. Leonidas Pantelides, Representative of the Greek Cypriot Community on the CMP; Mr. Hakki Muftuzade, Turkish Cypriot Member of the CMP (online) – “Making the Right to Know Effective: Lessons on Implementation and Cooperation”
• Dr. Luis Fondebrider, Forensic Anthropologist and independent consultant; co-founder of the Argentine Forensic Anthropology Team (EAAF) – “Effective and Sustainable Mechanisms for the clarification of the fate and whereabouts of Missing Persons”
• Prof. Gabriella Citroni, Adjunct Professor of International Human Rights Law at the University of Milano-Bicocca – “Searching for missing persons in transnational contexts”
• Dr. Mercedes Salado, Director for Eurasia and the Middle East, Argentine Forensic Anthropology Team (EAAF) – “Operational recommendations for the Search and Identification of Missing Persons. Integrated approaches”
• Dr. Melissa Robichon, Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Specialist in Forensics, International Committee of the Red Cross – “Families’ participation in the search for answers” (Online)
• Mr. Adnan Rizvic, Director of Data Systems and Data Coordination at the International Commission on Missing Persons (ICMP)
• Q&A

Moderator: Angelica Maria Guzman Velandia, ICRC Forensic Coordinator for Armenia

items.session4: Session IV – Families, Experiences – Achievements and Challenges
items.session4Details:
Voices, Memory, and Solidarity Across Contexts. From Institutional Perspectives to Families’ Experiences.

Introduction of Day 2’s focus on families’ perspectives, linking the institutional discussions of Day 1 to the experiences of those directly affected.

Introduction of PAARMP activities by Gor Muradyan, President of PAARMP
items.panel1: Panel I: Engagement with Authorities – Experiences Across Contexts
items.panel1Details: Family representatives from different contexts share their experience of interaction with authorities: access to institutions, recognition, responses received, barriers, good practices, and what they believe authorities should do differently.
items.voicesIntro: Voices of Families: Shared Experiences Across Contexts
items.voicesIntroDetails:
Keeping the humanitarian dimension at the forefront – The Role of Families.

Moderator’s introduction on the role of families in advocating for the issue of missing persons within peace processes and building understanding across communities.
items.armenianFamilies: Armenian Families’ Perspectives on International Visibility
items.armenianFamiliesDetails: A representative of an Armenian family association introduces their hopes and expectations regarding international visibility and its potential to raise awareness and bring the issue of missing persons onto international agendas and into negotiations.
items.panel2: Panel II: Keeping the Humanitarian Dimension at the Forefront – The Role of Families
items.panel2Details:
Family representatives from Cyprus, Kosovo, and Bosnia and Herzegovina share their efforts to gain international visibility and recognition, highlighting achievements, ongoing challenges, and the roles of authorities, civil society, and international actors.

The discussion explores how a humanitarian approach centered on families’ needs can help depoliticize the issue of missing persons and create opportunities for dialogue and action.
items.worldCafeDetails: Format: Rotating thematic discussions, with an Armenian family representative serving as the permanent facilitator at each table.

speakers.title: Speakers
speakers.lead: Conference speakers represent public institutions, international and humanitarian organizations, academia and civil society. The list is updated as participation and publication details are confirmed.

riepl.name: Dr. Michael Riepl
riepl.organization: Academy for European Human Rights Protection, University of Cologne
riepl.bio: Dr. Michael Riepl is an international lawyer, humanitarian practitioner and author. He studied law in Passau and Geneva and earned his doctorate from the University of Cologne. As a practitioner, he worked for the International Committee of the Red Cross in Geneva as well as Ukraine, Armenia, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Currently, he is a freelance author and a postdoctoral researcher at the Academy for European Human Rights Protection (University of Cologne), where he conducts research on international law, Eastern Europe and the Caucasus.

beruto.name: Gian Luca Beruto
beruto.role: Secretary-General; Director of the Special Projects Department
beruto.bio: Gian Luca Beruto currently holds the position of Secretary-General at the International Institute of Humanitarian Law, where he also serves as Director of the Special Projects Department. He has more than 20 years of professional management experience in UN agencies, international organizations and non-governmental agencies across Europe and Africa. With a multidisciplinary profile in international affairs and consolidated experience in project management, communication and training, his career has developed in areas including peacekeeping, conflict management, institution building, governance, disarmament, as well as assistance and protection of migrants and refugees.

citroni.name: Dr. Gabriella Citroni
citroni.role: Adjunct Professor of International Human Rights Law
citroni.bio: Gabriella Citroni is Adjunct Professor of International Human Rights Law at the University of Milano-Bicocca, Italy. She is also the former Chair-Rapporteur and member of the United Nations Working Group on Enforced or Involuntary Disappearances, an International Legal Advisor for the Latin American Federation of Associations for Relatives of the Detained-Disappeared (FEDEFAM) and a Senior Legal Advisor for TRIAL International. Her research focuses on international human rights law, and she cooperates with NGOs providing legal assistance to victims of serious human rights violations and their relatives in countries including Algeria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Nepal, Morocco, Colombia, Peru, Iraq, Honduras, Thailand and Mexico. She has been appointed as a consultant by the OSCE/ODIHR, the Council of Europe Commissioner for Human Rights and the ICRC on missing persons and enforced disappearance, and as an expert witness before the Inter-American Court of Human Rights. From 2003 to 2005 she was Legal Advisor to the Italian delegation during negotiations of the International Convention on the Protection of All Persons from Enforced Disappearance.

kirakosyan.name: Dr. Yeghishe Kirakosyan
kirakosyan.role: Co-Founder and Managing Partner; international law scholar
kirakosyan.bio: Dr. Kirakosyan is a scholar and educator with a strong academic background in international law. Since completing his PhD at Yerevan State University in 2006, he has served as an Assistant Professor at the Chair of European and International Law and taught at Yerevan State University and other leading universities in Armenia. For six years, until his resignation from public service in March 2025, he represented the Republic of Armenia before various international fora as the Representative on International Legal Matters, including before the International Court of Justice, the European Court of Human Rights, and international arbitral tribunals and foreign courts. He is Co-Founder and Managing Partner of Equity Law Partners. He is an ad hoc Judge of the European Court of Human Rights, a Member of the Permanent Court of Arbitration, a Member of the ICSID Panel of Arbitrators and Conciliators, a Licensed Attorney with the Chamber of Advocates of the Republic of Armenia since 2016, and a Member of the Council of the Arbitration and Mediation Center of Armenia.

gimigliano.name: Edoardo Gimigliano
gimigliano.role: Coordinator of the Special Projects Department
gimigliano.bio: Edoardo Gimigliano is the Coordinator of the Special Projects Department of the International Institute of Humanitarian Law and holds a master’s degree in international politics and diplomacy. His 8+ years of experience in the international law domain includes international legal research, training design and delivery, and international programmes management. With 100+ high-level awareness-raising initiatives carried out to date, his expertise mainly relates to the application and respect of IHL and international human rights law in humanitarian crises, including the protection of cultural heritage and essential services, gender-related aspects of humanitarian emergencies, missing persons, and disarmament processes.

melikyan.name: Anna Melikyan
melikyan.bio: Anna Melikyan is a Legal Expert with the NGO “Protection of Rights Without Borders”, Armenia. She works on documentation of violations during armed conflict as well as ensuring access to justice and human rights mechanisms for victims at national and international levels. This has included participation in fact-finding missions in 2020 and 2023 focused on captivity, detention and disappearance of both Armenian servicemen and civilians. She is also actively involved in advocacy to ensure better respect for the rights of missing persons and their families in law and in practice. Previously, she worked at the OSCE Mission to Moldova in the context of the settlement of the Transdniestrian conflict, and at the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights following an inter-ethnic conflict in Southern Kyrgyzstan. She has over 15 years of experience teaching human rights and humanitarian law. She holds an LL.M. from the Geneva Academy of International Humanitarian Law and Human Rights and a law degree from the Russian-Armenian (Slavonic) University.

fonderbider.name: Dr. Luis Fondebrider
fonderbider.bio: Forensic anthropologist with 42 years of experience in the search for missing persons across 66 countries. In 1984, he co-founded the Argentine Forensic Anthropology Team (EAAF), serving as its President from 2000 to 2021. He has provided expertise to the International Criminal Court (ICC), the International Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia (ICTY), United Nations Commissions of Inquiry, the Inter-American Court of Human Rights, the International Committee of the Red Cross, and various mechanisms for the search for missing persons. Among the countries where he has worked are Argentina, Peru, Colombia, Mexico, Guatemala, South Africa, DRC, Ethiopia, Libya, Bosnia, Kosovo, Sri Lanka, Iraq, Cyprus, Lebanon, Georgia, Timor-Leste, Indonesia and the Philippines. In 2006, he was awarded the rank of Chevalier of the Legion of Honour by the French government.

salado.name: Dr. Mercedes Salado
salado.role: Director for Eurasia and the Middle East
salado.bio: She has over 25 years of international experience in the forensic investigation, search and identification of missing persons in contexts of conflict, human rights violations, migration and other situations of violence. She has contributed to investigations, training and advisory missions worldwide, including Argentina, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Central African Republic, Colombia, Cyprus, Chile, Georgia, Guatemala, Iran, Iraq, Morocco, Mexico, Nepal, Panama, Peru, South Africa, Sudan, Chad, Thailand, Timor-Leste, Togo, Ukraine, Uruguay and Vietnam. She serves as an expert advisor to the UN Special Rapporteur on extrajudicial, summary or arbitrary executions, the ICRC, the Latin American Association of Forensic Anthropology (ALAF), and the American Academy of Forensic Sciences (AAFS).

guzman.name: Angelica Guzman
guzman.organization: International Committee of the Red Cross
guzman.bio: Angelica Guzman is a forensic anthropologist with more than ten years of experience with the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC). She has worked in the Americas, the Middle East, the Western Balkans, the Caucasus, South Asia and Nigeria, supporting the search for missing persons and the strengthening of national medico-legal systems. Before joining the ICRC, she worked as a sworn forensic expert within Colombia’s prosecution system, contributing to investigations into human rights violations, including cases brought before the Inter-American Court of Human Rights. She holds a master’s degree in Conflict Resolution and Peace Studies. She currently serves as the ICRC’s Forensic Coordinator in Armenia.

robichon.name: Melissa Robichon
robichon.role: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Specialist in Forensics
robichon.organization: International Committee of the Red Cross
robichon.bio: Melissa Robichon is a French neuropsychologist and clinical psychologist with specialized expertise in psychological trauma and emergency psychology. She began her career working in a psychiatric hospital, alongside serving as a trainer in psychology at university and hospital level. Since 2016, she has been engaged in the humanitarian sector with various INGOs. Her work has included the management and coordination of mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) programs, with a particular focus on psychosocial consequences of armed conflict, displacement and disappearance, including fieldwork in Iraq. Currently, Melissa works as a consultant with the ICRC, contributing to a forensic project aiming at strengthening the medicolegal system in Iraq and supporting medicolegal authorities engaging with families of missing persons.

pantelides.name: Leonidas Pantelides
pantelides.role: Representative of the Greek Cypriot Community
pantelides.organization: Committee on Missing Persons in Cyprus (CMP)
pantelides.bio: Leonidas Pantelides was appointed Representative of the Greek Cypriot Community on the Committee on Missing Persons in Cyprus in May 2019. A retired ambassador of the Republic of Cyprus, he served in Stockholm, Athens, Moscow, Geneva and Washington, DC. He also directed the President’s Diplomatic Office and worked on Middle East affairs. Before entering diplomacy, he was a university lecturer. He holds a PhD in philosophy and has published two books, including a book on the Cyprus problem co-authored with Ahmet Sözen.

muftuzade.name: Hakki Müftüzade
muftuzade.organization: Committee on Missing Persons in Cyprus (CMP)
muftuzade.bio: Hakki Müftüzade was appointed Turkish Cypriot Member of the Committee on Missing Persons in Cyprus on 1 January 2021. He has extensive diplomatic experience, including service as Special Advisor to two Turkish Cypriot leaders between 2001 and 2010 and as Representative of the Turkish Cypriot community in the United Kingdom from 1996 to 2001. He previously assisted Rüstem Tatar, then the Turkish Cypriot Member of the Committee. He has also contributed to educational and sporting organizations. He completed a degree in Policy Making and Administration at the University of Essex, United Kingdom.

gentile.name: Pierre Gentile
gentile.organization: Committee on Missing Persons in Cyprus (CMP)
gentile.bio: Pierre Gentile was nominated as the UN representative on the Committee on Missing Persons in Cyprus in September 2024. Previously, he led the Center for Social Integration of Refugees in Lausanne, Switzerland. He worked for the ICRC from 1996 to 2019, including more than ten years in field operations in the Balkans, Afghanistan, Latin America, Africa and the Middle East. In 2007, he established the Protection of Civilian Population unit at ICRC headquarters in Geneva. In 2014, he was appointed head of the Protection Division and the Central Tracing Agency.
